comments.author: shenghanzhe
comments.body_html:
This mod boosts and tweaks all headsets in Escape from Tarkov to make them much more powerful.

  • Greatly increases ambient noise reduction (quieter background sounds)
  • Makes all headset audio much louder
  • Boosts low, mid, and high frequencies
  • Makes footsteps much more noticeable
  • Slightly increases the distance at which you can hear sounds

The goal is to make headsets feel much more effective and dramatic, so you can hear important sounds (like footsteps) more easily, like it was before in SPT 3.9

comments.author: shenghanzhe
comments.body_html:
They should work fine together. However, it’s best to load DeDistortionizer after this mod.

DeDistortionizer sets distortion to 0.01 for specific headsets. This mod increases distortion by 20%, so if it runs after DeDistortionizer, the value becomes 0.012 (slightly higher, but still lower than the original BSG values).

If this mod loads first (which is usually the case), DeDistortionizer will overwrite the distortion value to 0.01.
Still needs some testing though

comments.author: shenghanzhe
comments.body_html:
In the old version there were gain adjustments for each low, mid, and high frequency. I merged them into one adjustment so EQBandGain multiplies the gain of all 3 frequency bands together. It acts as a “global gain multiplier” for all frequencies. If a headset has:

Band1Gain = 2.0 → becomes 2.0 × 1.75 = 3.5 Band2Gain = 1.5 → becomes 1.5 × 1.75 = 2.625 Band3Gain = 3.0 → becomes 3.0 × 1.75 = 5.25

EQBandGain - multiplier for gain of all bands (makes them louder/quieter) EQBandFrequency - multiplier for center frequencies of all bands (shifts frequencies up/down) EQBandQ - multiplier for Q/bandwidth of all bands (narrower or wider bands)

comments.author: shenghanzhe
comments.body_html:
Hi
Sorry for the late reply..
Higher number meaning more reduction doesn’t apply unless it’s stated so.
Some default values have a negative value, so by multiplying it by 2 we actually even more decrease it’s value sent to the compressor.
There are no minimum/maximum values. Decimals can be used and actually it’s better to increase or decrease values by a decimal.
